newsitem.title: USA: Russia to become member of Paris creditors club.
newsitem.headline: Russia to become member of Paris creditors club.

text.p: Russia is to join the Paris Club of creditor nations, President Bill Clinton announced on Friday as he met President Boris Yeltsin ahead of a summit of industrialised nations in Denver.

Clinton called it a "happy development." A statement by the Paris Club said negotiations on Russian entry, long sought by Moscow, were concluded on Friday, but still needed formal ratification by the whole group.
Clinton appeared delighted at the deal.
"We...have another happy development here today," he said with a beaming Yeltsin sitting beside him. "Russia and the Paris Club have just completed their negotiations."
Clinton said this meant Russia would "now be a partner with the other members" in trying to promote global economic growth by relieving the debt of developing nations that adopt reforms.
"What you see here is a sweeping integration of Russia into the major decision-making networks of the world in a way that is very positive for the rest of us," Clinton said.
Russia, which inherited both the debts and the obligations of the former Soviet Union, has won a series of deals to reschedule Soviet-era debts.
It wanted to join the Paris Club as a creditor in an effort to win repayment of some debts extended to Soviet allies, most of them in the developing world.
Washington has also pledged to support Russian entry to the World Trade Organisation and the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development.
But U.S. officials say Moscow has not yet taken all the necessary steps for admission to these bodies.
Asked if he wanted the Group of Seven -- the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Canada and Japan -- to include Russia, Clinton said this was already effectively the case.
"Russia is fully included," he said. "This is the first time we've ever had a meeting that Russia was included in from beginning to end."
U.S. officials have gone out of their way to emphasise Moscow's enhanced role at the Denver summit, and it is being officially called "The Summit of the Eight."

But Yeltsin is still excluded from one session here -- a discussion on financial policy on Saturday afternoon -- and Japan at least is reluctant to see it fully integrated into the group at this stage.
In another gesture to underline his support for Yeltsin's full inclusion, Clinton arranged for him to lead off the discussion at the first event of the gathering, a working dinner on Friday evening.

As well as talking about Russia's integration in international financial institutions, U.S. officials said Clinton and Yeltsin continued a dialogue on NATO's planned expansion and its new friendly relationship with Moscow.
The Paris Club said the deal letting Russia join its ranks still needed formal agreement by the whole group.
In a statement, it said its chairman, Christian Noyer, had finalised the deal with Mikhail Kasyanov, Russia's vice minister of finance, in Denver on Friday.
The two agreed that Russia would join "through the application of realistic broad adjustment to make Russian claims comparable with Paris Club members' claims vis-a-vis debtor countries."

"This understanding lies on a differentiation between debtors with a higher adjustment for the poorest countries, and taking account country specificities, with a view to ensure the financial sustainability of all debtors," it said.
